headline.technical: Bloomberg reported AI skepticism is crushing stocks worldwide; S&P 500 closed -3.70% and Nasdaq Composite -5.28% on 2026-11-20, with VIX at 35.89.
headline.layman: Worries about AI spending hit stocks around the world. US shares fell sharply on Friday, and the market's 'fear gauge' jumped.

global.title: AI selloff spreads across global markets

status.technical: Reuters said the S&P 500 and Dow ended in correction. S&P 500 1d -3.70%, 5d -8.61%; RSI14 24.7. Asia-Pacific fell 8.3% for the week per Business Standard. VIX closed at 35.89.
status.layman: Stocks fell sharply around the world this week. Reuters said US shares ended in a 'correction', a drop of 10% or more from a high. The VIX, a measure of market fear, hit 35.89.

consequence.technical: Rediker (Bloomberg) called the selloff a 'healthy' correction; Curnutt warned the overlap of the AI trade and the economy could leave markets vulnerable to further declines.
consequence.layman: One expert called the drop 'healthy'. Another said the AI trade is now so tied to the wider economy that markets could stay shaky.

impact.technical: Reuters instant view said Nasdaq fell 5% but investors still believe in AI. WSJ reported investors rushing into value stocks; Bitcoin is on its longest weekly losing streak since May 2022.
impact.layman: Tech shares took the biggest hit. Some investors moved into cheaper 'value' stocks. Bitcoin also kept falling.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after S&P 500 falls of this size, next day rose 48% of 155 times and next 5 days rose 58% of 152 times.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after drops like this, the S&P 500 rose the next day about 48% of the time, and over the next 5 days 58% of the time.

regions.title: Americas: Wall Street drops into correction

status.technical: AP News reported the S&P 500 sank 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite went negative for the year. Nasdaq Composite 1d -5.28%, Dow Jones 1d -1.93%, Russell 2000 1d -2.76%, TSX 1d -2.47%.
status.layman: US stocks fell hard on Friday, and the Nasdaq is now down for the year. Canada's main index also fell.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported chipmakers led the plunge. If the AI doubts persist, tech-heavy indices stay exposed; Reuters said the S&P 500 and Dow closed in correction.
consequence.layman: Chip companies led the fall. If worries about AI spending continue, tech-heavy markets could stay under pressure.

impact.technical: Nvidia fell 14% (CNBC), per CNBC its longest weekly losing streak since 2008. Reuters reported the Canadian dollar fell for a third straight week; Reuters said the TSX had its longest daily losing streak since 2024.
impact.layman: Nvidia, a leading chip maker, fell 14%. Canada's currency and stock market were also weak.

outlook.technical: Base rates: after big one-day falls, Nasdaq next day rose 50% of 171 times; S&P 500 next 5 days rose 58% of 152 times. These are not predictions.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after falls like this, the Nasdaq rose the next day about half the time (50%).

regions.title: Europe: FTSE 100 and bourses slip with tech

status.technical: Morningstar reported the FTSE 100 fell as the global tech selloff deepened. FTSE 100 1d -1.02%, 5d -5.10%. DAX 1d -1.06% on 2026-11-19.
status.layman: European markets slipped as the tech selloff spread. The UK's FTSE 100 fell about 1% on Friday.

consequence.technical: WSJ reported eurozone wage growth accelerated but remains modest. If pay growth stays modest, that is one fewer inflation concern, per the headline.
consequence.layman: Pay in the eurozone grew faster but is still modest.

impact.technical: Euronews reported Lufthansa plans 1,000 job cuts in Frankfurt and Munich as the Iran war slows its turnaround. Euronews said Commerzbank welcomed UniCredit's commitments after a Berlin agreement.
impact.layman: Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs. Commerzbank welcomed UniCredit's promises to keep it listed in Frankfurt.

outlook.technical: Base rates: after falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, FTSE 100 next 5 days rose 65% of 158 times. Base rates are not predictions.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after similar falls, the FTSE 100 rose over the next 5 days about 65% of the time.

status.technical: Business Standard reported MSCI's Asia-Pacific index fell 3.2% on Friday and was down 8.3% for the week. Bloomberg said Taiwan stocks headed for their worst week since 1991 and Hong Kong stocks fell 20% from their 2026 high. TAIEX 1d -4.40% on 2026-11-19.
status.layman: Asian stocks had their worst week since 2020. Taiwan's market had its worst week since 1991, according to Bloomberg. India was the exception.

consequence.technical: Business Standard said Nifty 50 ended at 25,800.60, up 1.12 per cent on Friday, on foreign inflows, a rupee rally and cooling crude oil prices. If oil stays lower, Mint said the Nifty could test a record high.
consequence.layman: India's market rose on money coming in from foreign investors, a stronger rupee and cheaper oil.

impact.technical: Nikkei Asia reported SK Hynix will become Kioxia's top shareholder. Bloomberg reported yen and franc haven demand as the dollar slipped. Tokyo Electron -7.06% (1d), SoftBank Group -14.48% (1d).
impact.layman: Investors bought the yen and Swiss franc as safe places. Big Japanese chip-related stocks fell sharply.

outlook.technical: Base rates: after big falls, TAIEX next day rose 60% of 151 times; Hang Seng next 5 days rose 47% of 173 times. These are base rates, not predictions.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after big drops like this, Taiwan's market rose the next day about 60% of the time.

drivers.title: AI spending doubts and Anthropic's IPO

status.technical: Business Standard reported Anthropic shares fell nearly 9 per cent after a record $93.5 billion IPO. WSJ said the AI wipeout reached $4 Trillion. Straits Times reported many IPO plans were pushed to 2027.
status.layman: Anthropic's shares fell after a record share sale, and other AI-related companies delayed their own.

consequence.technical: If AI financing worries persist, Mint reported asset-backed debt sales topped the post-GFC record, so AI infrastructure builders rely on debt markets; Rediker noted rising financing risk.
consequence.layman: Many AI builders borrow heavily. If doubts grow, that borrowing could become harder.

impact.technical: DayOne paused US IPO plans on data centre and market concerns (Straits Times). Reuters reported Wall Street banks expect $1 billion in fees from the Anthropic and SpaceX IPOs.
impact.layman: A Singapore data-centre firm paused its IPO. Banks still earn fees from the big listings.

outlook.technical: Base rates after sharp S&P 500 falls: next 5 days rose 58% of 152 times. Not a prediction.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after sharp falls, the S&P 500 rose over the following 5 days about 58% of the time.

status.technical: CNBC said Nvidia fell 14% and had its longest weekly losing streak since 2008. FT reported an SEC probe into its accounting after Jensen Huang's resignation. Nvidia -14.01% (1d), -22.92% (5d).
status.layman: Nvidia fell 14%. The FT said a US regulator is looking into its accounting after its CEO resigned.

consequence.technical: If the probe and Senate scrutiny continue, Nvidia remains in focus; CNBC said Huang will testify publicly before a Senate banking panel. Bessent told CNBC chip export policy is unchanged.
consequence.layman: Nvidia's former CEO will speak to a Senate panel. The US Treasury chief said chip export policy has not changed.

impact.technical: CNBC reported a massive bearish trade in chip stocks, with options traders betting on further falls.
impact.layman: Some traders are betting chip stocks fall further.

outlook.technical: Base rates: Nasdaq next day rose 50% of 171 times after similar falls; not a prediction.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after falls like this, the Nasdaq rose the next day about half the time.

status.technical: Mint said gold slid for a fifth day as a hawkish Federal Reserve signaled more interest-rate hikes. US 10-year Treasury yield closed 4.91, 1d -2.77%. WSJ said the Dollar Index rose 0.42% this week to 98.75.
status.layman: Mint said the Fed signaled more rate hikes. Government borrowing rates fell on Friday.

consequence.technical: Mint reported the dollar weakened as a Fed-fueled rally stalled and lower US yields helped the yen. If yields keep falling, that may ease pressure on haven currencies.
consequence.layman: Lower US rates helped the yen. A weaker dollar can help countries that borrow in dollars.

impact.technical: Gold fell 3.98% in a day and Gold -8.94% over 5 days; Mint reported its biggest weekly decline since March.
impact.layman: Gold had its worst week since March.

outlook.technical: Base rates for the 10-year yield are in the market data; evidence is thin on direction. Not a prediction.
outlook.layman: Evidence is thin on where rates go next.

drivers.title: Oil falls on rising Middle East supply

status.technical: WSJ reported crude futures fell for a third straight week as Middle East supply outweighed concerns about strikes. Brent crude oil closed at 89.87, 1d -2.29%, 1m -20.59%.
status.layman: Oil prices fell for a third straight week because more oil is coming from the Middle East.

consequence.technical: Business Standard said recovery in Strait of Hormuz shipments eased supply fears. Mint reported India's rally was helped by cooling crude oil prices.

impact.technical: Euronews reported soaring fuel costs linked to the Iran war weighed on Lufthansa. FT said Trump is considering new Iran strikes.
impact.layman: Fuel costs hurt Lufthansa. Possible new US strikes on Iran add uncertainty.

outlook.technical: Base rates for Brent are in the market data; they are not predictions.

status.technical: CNBC said Trump vowed to stop US companies building data centers abroad and threatened a tremendous tax. Al Jazeera reported lawmakers want tougher AI chip rules. CNBC said US-China trade, Taiwan and tech tensions remain unresolved.
status.layman: President Trump threatened a heavy tax on data centers built abroad. Lawmakers want tougher chip rules. Tensions with China are unresolved.

consequence.technical: If rules tighten, chip makers and data-centre builders could face higher costs, as the notes suggest; evidence is thin on size.
consequence.layman: Stricter rules could raise costs for chip and data-center companies.

impact.technical: Taiwan and Korean chip names fell: TSMC -4.76% (1d), Samsung Electronics -7.01% (1d).

outlook.technical: Base rates: TAIEX next day rose 60% of 151 times after similar falls; not a prediction.

events.title: RBI 4-day Variable Rate Repo auction
events.technical: RBI will conduct a Variable Rate Repo auction on Monday, November 23, 2026, in view of near-term liquidity conditions.
events.layman: India's central bank will lend money to banks for four days to manage cash supply.

events.title: RBI Treasury bill auctions (91, 182, 364-day)
events.technical: RBI announced auctions of 91-Day, 182-Day and 364-Day Treasury Bills on November 25, 2026 (Wednesday).
events.layman: India's government will sell short-term bonds to investors.

companyEffects.technical: CNBC said Nvidia plunged 14%, its longest weekly losing streak since 2008; FT reported an SEC accounting probe.
companyEffects.layman: Nvidia fell 14% and faces a regulator's probe, weighing on US indices.

companyEffects.technical: Business Standard reported shares fell nearly 9 per cent after a record $93.5 billion IPO; Guardian said it did not buoy the Nasdaq.
companyEffects.layman: Anthropic's shares fell after its record share sale, adding to tech worries.

companyEffects.technical: CNBC said Zscaler jumped 18% on a report CrowdStrike is in talks to buy it.
companyEffects.layman: Zscaler rose 18% on a report that CrowdStrike may buy it.
